item.title: Permit B: renewal and requirements in the Nidvaldo
item.description: How to renew the residence permit B in the Canton of Nidvaldo: administrative procedure, mandatory documents, duration of validity and contacts of the administration.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Permit B is renewable to continue legally residing in Switzerland - Procedure managed by the Nidwalden cantonal administration, not federal offices - Renewal requires submission of documents within specific deadlines
## Key facts - **What**: Permit B (renewable residence) - Renewability: Yes, renewable according to federal migration regulations - Who manages: Nidwalden cantonal administration - Regulatory level: Federal (SEM) and cantonal (administrative execution) - Validity: Temporary, subject to periodic renewal
### What is the Permit B The Permit B is the legal status that allows a foreign person to reside continuously in Switzerland. It differs from Permit L (short duration, up to 1 year) and Permit C (settlement, generally longer duration). Crucial aspect: Permit B is renewable, meaning the holder can continue residing beyond the initial validity period, following administrative renewal procedures.
In the Canton of Nidwalden, as in all 26 Swiss cantons, the administrative management of residence permits is the responsibility of the local cantonal administration, while the basic regulations and general principles come from the federal level through the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM).
### Duration of Permit B and Renewal Cycle The duration of Permit B is not unlimited: it expires after a predetermined period that varies depending on individual circumstances. When the permit is about to expire, it is mandatory to start the renewal procedure with the Nidwalden cantonal administration. The renewal must be requested before the document expires, otherwise the right of residence automatically lapses.
The renewal procedure is not automatic: it requires personal initiative from the holder and the submission of updated documentation, in accordance with the indications of the cantonal migration office. A fundamental element is the [mandatory LAMal coverage (health insurance)](nav:health), required by law for all residents in Switzerland. Without this document, the renewal cannot proceed. Response times and specific requirements vary slightly from canton to canton, although the federal regulation provides the common basic framework. ### Required documents and administrative procedure
The procedure for renewing the B residence permit in Nidwalden follows a standardized administrative process. The applicant must contact the competent cantonal office (usually called the Migration Office, Demography Office, or equivalent, depending on the internal organization of the canton) and submit a formal renewal request using the official forms.
The documents generally required for renewal include: original B permit or certified copy, completed renewal application form, proof of current residence (extract from the residents' register or rental contract, utility bills), income documentation or proof of means of subsistence, copy of valid passport or identity document, and certification of active enrollment in the LAMal.
The LAMal is mandatory by law for all residents in Switzerland, including B permit holders. The insurance must be taken out within 3 months of arrival in Switzerland and maintained continuously throughout the entire stay in the country. Confirmation of active enrollment and current coverage is an essential element at the time of submitting the renewal request.
### Competencies: distinction between federal and cantonal levels
A critical aspect concerns the correct attribution of administrative competencies. The State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) at the federal level defines the general regulations, establishes the categories of permits and the basic requirements for foreigners. However, the concrete execution — the reception of applications, the verification of documentation, the communication of approval or refusal, the issuance of the renewal — is entrusted to the cantonal administrations.
In Nidwalden, as in all cantons, the competent cantonal office is structured to manage these procedures directly. It is not possible to request the renewal directly from the federal SEM; the correct way is always through the cantonal administration of your place of residence. This decentralized structure is characteristic of the Swiss migration system and remains consistent in all 26 cantons, ensuring uniform normative treatment while maintaining local administrative management.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### Practical guide: step-by-step to renew the B permit
For those who hold a B residence permit in the Canton of Nidwalden, renewal is a mandatory administrative step. Here are the main steps of the procedure:
1. Check the expiry date Carefully check the expiry date indicated on the B permit. Mark this date in your calendar and start gathering the necessary documents at least 2-3 months before the expiry date to avoid critical situations and allow the cantonal administration to process the application without time pressure.
2. Gather all required documentation Prepare a folder with all the necessary documents: valid passport, extract from the residents' register or updated rental contract, income documentation (employer's certificate, income statement), certificate of active enrollment in LAMal, and any other document required by the cantonal administration of Nidwalden.
3. Contact the cantonal migration office Check the reception hours of the competent cantonal office and the method of submission (in person at the offices, by mail, or via an online platform if available). Some cantons also offer appointment booking for preliminary consultations.
4. Submit the official renewal request Submit the completed application form and documentation to the indicated office, following the communicated methods. It is essential to keep a copy of all submitted documents and, if sent by mail, send everything by registered mail with return receipt.
**5. Wait for administrative processing** The cantonal administration verifies the completeness of the documentation and compliance with legal requirements. Processing times generally range from 4 to 8 weeks, depending on the office's workload and seasonality (peak periods in spring/summer).
6. Pick up the new permit Once the application is approved, the new B residence permit is ready for collection at the cantonal office of Nidwalden. It will be provided with a new expiry date and will have the same legal validity as the previous one.
### The crucial role of LAMal in renewal
It is not possible to underestimate the importance of [mandatory health insurance LAMal](nav:health) in the renewal procedure. An essential condition is active and continuous enrollment in a recognized health insurance. Without valid health coverage, the renewal of the B residence permit will be automatically rejected by the cantonal administration.
LAMal premiums are calculated on an individual basis (per capita) and vary depending on the canton of residence and the tariff region. The Canton of Nidwalden has its own specific rates and offers cantonal subsidies for premium reduction, aimed at residents with low or medium incomes. Always check the status of your enrollment at least 30 days before submitting the renewal request.
For precise and up-to-date information on the procedure in Nidwalden, contact the cantonal administration directly. The contact details of the competent office (address, phone, hours, booking methods) are published and updated on the official website of the Canton of Nidwalden.

item.title: Residence permit B canton Vaud: requirements and renewal
item.description: How to renew the B permit in the Vaud? What are the requirements? Practical guide to the procedures, necessary documents and deadlines for the renewal of the residence.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The B permit is a renewable residence permit for foreign workers in Switzerland - Managed by the federal SEM and the Vaud canton migration office - Renewal should be initiated 1–2 months before expiration - Requirements: employment contract, social security contributions, mandatory LAMal insurance
## Key facts - **What**: Renewable residence permit B for foreigners working in Switzerland - Who: State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) and cantonal migration office - Duration: Renewable, usually annual or biennial depending on the canton - Procedure: Submit application 1–2 months before expiration - Requirements: Employment contract, social security contributions (AVS/AI/IPG 5.3% employee), active LAMal
In the Swiss system of foreign permits, the residence permit B represents the most common category for those working in the country. It is a renewable authorization that allows foreign citizens to reside and work in Switzerland permanently, while still being subject to periodic verification.
Management is divided between the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) at the federal level and local cantonal authorities. In the canton of Vaud, as in other cantons, the cantonal migration office processes applications, issues, and renews permits according to federal and cantonal laws.
### The B permit: basic features
The B permit allows foreign citizens to reside continuously in Switzerland, provided they maintain regular employment and meet social security requirements. Unlike the L permit (short duration, up to 1 year), the B permit is renewable and is intended for those who wish to settle in the country for a medium to long period.
There is no single federal model: each canton, within the federal regulatory framework, sets specific durations and procedures. In Vaud, the procedure follows standard Swiss criteria, but the competent offices and organizational details are local. The duration of the permit — annual or biennial — is communicated in the official document and depends on the personal situation and the sector of work.
### Who requests the B permit
The residence permit B is mainly requested by foreign workers who intend to reside and work in Switzerland for a medium to long period (over 1 year). It is not automatic: it must be requested by the employer together with the worker before the start of the activity, or renewed periodically if already in possession.
Anyone holding a B permit expiring in the canton of Vaud must submit a renewal application through the competent office. The permit does not renew automatically: if an application is not submitted before expiration, the permit lapses and the stay becomes illegal.
### The role of the employer
In the canton of Vaud, as in all of Switzerland, the employer plays a central role in the permit process. During the renewal of the permit, the employer provides statements on the continuation of the employment contract, the salaries paid, and the employment situation. Salaries and social security contributions (AVS, AI, unemployment) are monitored by the authorities, and periods of non-payment result in rejection of the renewal. To learn more about AVS, AI, and unemployment contributions, [consult our comprehensive guide to social security](nav:pension). Without the involvement and support of the employer, renewal of the B permit is practically impossible. ### Renewal procedure and general requirements
The renewal of the B permit must generally be initiated 1–2 months before the expiry date. There is no single national date; each cantonal office sets its own processing times. Those who forget to renew and continue to work illegally expose themselves and their employer to administrative sanctions and potential revocation of authorizations.
The fundamental requirements for maintaining an active B permit include: - A valid employment contract with an employer resident in Switzerland - Regular payment of social security contributions (AVS/AI/IPG, unemployment contributions, accident insurance) - Subscription and maintenance of health insurance (LAMal) — mandatory within 3 months of arrival and to be maintained continuously for all residents - No legal impediments (relevant criminal records, tax debts)
### The role of social security and insurance
Those working in Switzerland automatically pay 5.3% of AVS/AI/IPG contributions on the employee part (the employer pays a total of 10.6%). These contributions are tracked by employers and communicated to migration offices during permit renewal. A gap in social security contributions results in the rejection of the renewal application.
The LAMal health insurance is private and based on per capita premiums: the premium depends on the canton, the tariff region, age, and the chosen deductible. It is neither a tax nor a salary contribution — it is a policy taken out directly with an insurer. The migration office verifies that all residents have active coverage. Those without LAMal at the time of the renewal request will see their application rejected. If you wish to [consult the LAMal health insurance options for the canton of Vaud](nav:health), dedicated tools are available for your canton of residence.
### Processing times and cantonal checks
Processing a renewal application generally takes 4–8 weeks. During this period, the Vaud migration office verifies the regularity of the employment contract, social security payments, insurance coverage, and any situations of tax insolvency. If everything is in order, the new permit is issued and notified in writing. If elements are missing, the office requests additional information or communicates a motivated rejection.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### How to start the renewal process in Vaud
Step 1: Check the expiry of your permit The number and expiry date are visible on the physical document of the permit. Do not wait until the last day: renewal takes time and involves administrative procedures.
**Step 2: Gather the documents** Prepare: - Official application form of the canton of Vaud (available on the website of the cantonal migration office) - Copy of the current employment contract - Latest pay slips (last 3–6 months, as requested) - Tax regularity certificate (if requested by the canton) - Proof of active LAMal coverage (insurer's document) - Valid passport or identity document
Step 3: Submit the application The application can generally be submitted in two ways: - In person at the migration office of the canton of Vaud - By post, if the canton allows it (check the official website)
The complete form and the payment of any administrative fees follow the instructions of the local office.
Step 4: Wait and renew Processing the application generally takes 4–8 weeks. The office will notify the outcome by letter or email. If approved, the new permit will be delivered or collected at the office.
### Where to go in the canton of Vaud The canton of Vaud has a Service de la population — Office de la migration with offices in Lausanne and other locations. The exact coordinates, opening hours, and submission methods are available on the canton's official website (Vaud canton domain, Migration and Population section).
It is not advisable to rely on private agencies for renewal: the procedure is managed directly and free of charge by the cantonal office. External agencies may charge unnecessary fees.
### Special situations If your employment contract ends before the permit expires, you must immediately inform the migration office. A period of unemployment does not automatically renew the permit: you must demonstrate that you remain insured in social security (with unemployed status at the employment office).
If the renewal application is rejected, you have the right to appeal within 30 days to the competent cantonal authority. The reasons for rejection are nevertheless communicated in writing.

item.title: AVS and complementary services: St. Gallen guide
item.description: How the first pillar works in the Canton of St. Gallen. Learn about the role of the cantonal compensation fund, pension calculation, contribution gaps and supplementary benefits for the living minimum.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - The AVS is the foundation of Swiss social security: mandatory, financed with 5.3% contributions for employees (10.6% total with employer). - The cantonal compensation fund records the contributions and calculates the annuity based on the years of contribution and the amounts paid. - Supplementary benefits cover the minimum living allowance when the AVS income is not sufficient: regulated by the Canton of St. Gallen and subsidized by the Confederation.
## Key facts - **What**: First pillar of Swiss social security (AVS/AHV), mandatory for all workers - When: Registration from the first day of work until retirement (currently 65 years for men, 64 for women, with reform in progress) - Where: Managed by the Canton of St. Gallen Clearing House and UFAS/BSV at federal level - Who: Employers, employees, cantonal administration (complementary services) - Amount: Contribution rate 5.3% employees, calculation of annuity based on years and amounts credited to the insurance account
The AVS represents the fundamental pillar of Swiss social security. In the Canton of St. Gallen, as in every canton, the operational management is the responsibility of the local compensation fund: the entity that registers members, credits the contributions paid monthly by employers and employees, maintains the individual insurance account and, upon reaching retirement age, calculates and pays the pension.
The system is mandatory for any ### Calculation of the AVS annuity: mechanics and determining factors
The AVS pension is not a refund of contributions paid, but a benefit calculated according to a federal formula that takes into account two essential elements: the number of years of contribution from the first job until retirement age, and the average amount of annual contributions during the entire career. For a full income and not reduced, 44 years of contributions (for men) are required. If years are missing, the annuity is reduced proportionally: each missing year results in a reduction calculated on the basis of the federal formula.
The compensation fund of the Canton of St. Gallen carries out the calculation using the data stored in the personal insurance account. The process starts at least 3 months before the desired retirement age. The fund estimates the average coordinated income (i.e. the average salary during the career), applies the federal formula and informs the retiree of the result — normally 4 weeks before the start date of the pension. It is at this time that the taxpayer finds out if gaps result or if the coverage is complete.
An important element: the taxpayer can request the deferral of the pension up to 5 years after the retirement age. This choice significantly increases the monthly benefit amount, as years of contribution are added and a federal surcharge factor is applied.

The steps are as follows: 1. Contact the cantonal clearing house. The first step is to notify the Canton of St. Gallen's compensation fund of your intention to retire and the expected date. This contact can be by phone, email or personal visit. During this communication, request the official AVS pension application form and provide personal data, AVS number and desired pension start date. 2. **Fill in the official application **. The cash register provides a standardized form that must be filled in each part. The form must state if you intend to continue a work activity during retirement (this information affects the calculation of the pension) and if you want to request the deferral of the pension to obtain a higher monthly amount. 3. item.title: Buying a house in San Gallo: mortgage and taxes
item.description: Guide to buying real estate in Switzerland: mortgage, own funds, transfer tax and step-by-step procedures for buyers in the Canton of St. Gallen.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Real estate purchase is one of the main investments in the life of a Swiss resident - Mortgage requires own funds of at least 20% of the purchase price - Transfer tax, notary fees, and tax deductibility of interest affect the total budget
## Key facts - **What**: Purchase of real estate property in Switzerland - Where: Canton of St. Gallen (and Swiss national market) - Who: Swiss residents, borrowers with verifiable income - Minimum own funds: At least 20% of the purchase price (bank standard) - Deductibility: Mortgage interest is tax-deductible at the federal and cantonal levels
The Swiss real estate market follows economic dynamics that vary from canton to canton. When planning to buy a home, the first step is to understand the structural factors that influence prices: location, size of the building, condition of the property, proximity to public services, and access to transportation infrastructure.
At the national level, the Swiss housing market is regulated by federal laws on land ownership. However, each canton has its own jurisdiction over real estate taxation, including transfer taxes (stamp duties), which vary significantly depending on the jurisdiction. In the Canton of St. Gallen, as in every canton, the price of a property depends on general economic factors — bank interest rates, credit availability, market demand — and local factors such as demographic growth and economic development. Mortgage interest rates are set by banks and follow the trend of the Swiss National Bank (SNB), which guides the country's monetary policy.
### Provision and financial stability
Before applying for a mortgage, it is crucial to assess your overall financial sustainability. Switzerland provides three levels of provision: AHV (old-age and survivors' insurance), BVG (occupational pension fund), and the third pillar, which affect the available assets for purchase. A relevant aspect: funds from the occupational pension fund (BVG) can be partially withdrawn for the purchase of a first home. This operation allows increasing the available own funds but must be carefully evaluated in relation to the future old-age pension.
Health insurance coverage (LAMal) is mandatory for all Swiss residents. Premiums vary by canton and risk region and must be considered in the monthly budget when assessing whether a mortgage is sustainable. Also, ordinary and extraordinary maintenance costs of the property must be planned for the long term. The mortgage is the main financing tool for buying real estate in Switzerland. Banks typically require own funds equal to at least 20% of the purchase price. This percentage is a well-established standard throughout Switzerland, although some institutions may offer slightly different conditions with higher interest rates. Mortgages are offered by banks in two main forms: fixed rate (the rate remains unchanged for the entire duration, usually 5, 10, or 15 years, providing certainty on monthly installments) and variable rate (the rate changes according to market interest rates, which involves the risk of increased installments but potential savings if rates fall).

item.title: Bally, in Caslano the umpteenth cut of staff
item.description: Regent LP cuts 25 administrative posts at Bally Caslano. Employees drop from ~100 to 54. Agreed in progress, 60.5M losses in 2024.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Regent LP cuts 25 administrative jobs at Bally Caslano - Employees from ~100 (June 2024) to 54 today, activity halted for months - Losses: -60.5M (2024), -27.7M (2025); buyer search ongoing
## Key facts - **What**: Collective dismissal of 25 administrative employees - When: Announced by Transliq AG (ongoing moratorium procedure) - Where: Caslano, Bally plant in Ticino - Who: Regent LP (owner since August 2024), Transliq AG (moratorium manager) - Employees: 100 in June 2024 → 54 today at the plant - Net loss 2024: -60.5 million CHF (Ebitda) - Activity: Production halted for months; sale process ongoing
Regent LP, the American fund that acquired Bally in August 2024, continues to downsize the workforce of the historic luxury shoe brand. Transliq AG, in charge of the moratorium procedure, has announced a new possible collective dismissal involving 25 administrative employees in Caslano. A procedure that may not be the last: in less than two years, Bally has recorded collective dismissals, store closures, and two failed attempts to acquire the brand.
The workforce reduction has been drastic. From the approximately 100 employees present in June 2024, today there are 54 at the plant. A dozen still work in Swiss stores. Before Regent LP's arrival, Bally employed a total of 169 people in Switzerland, with 122 in Caslano, the heart of Ticino production.
### The financial situation
The numbers reflect a deep crisis. In 2023, Bally reported a positive Ebitda of 43.5 million francs. In 2024, the result plummeted to -60.5 million. In 2025, losses were reduced to -27.7 million, but the operating cash flow remained negative at 16.45 million francs. These figures show that the brand continues to burn resources despite continuous workforce cuts.
Production activity in Caslano has been halted for months. As part of the moratorium procedure, a sale process of the operational activity, including the plant, facilities, employment contracts, and lease agreements, has been initiated. The stated goal of Transliq AG is to allow the resumption of production and safeguard local jobs. However, the brand is not included in the sale operation: two previous attempts to acquire it have failed, further complicating the path to a positive solution. ### The implications for the Swiss labor market
The Bally crisis reflects a broader challenge for the Swiss labor market: the vulnerability of traditional companies in the face of global changes in the luxury and manufacturing sectors. With 54 employees remaining at the Caslano plant and another 25 potentially at risk, the dispute directly affects unemployment in the Ticino canton and the employment basin of the Lugano area.
The ongoing concordat procedure is a tool provided by the Swiss Code of Obligations that allows a company to negotiate a solution to avoid bankruptcy. In this case, Transliq AG acts as the curator of the moratorium, seeking a buyer willing to take over the operational activity. This means that, theoretically, jobs could be saved if the sale is successful. However, the fact that the brand is not included in the operation creates uncertainty: a buyer might only take over the production of shoes for third parties, without the prestige and added value of the historic Bally brand.
### What does this mean for the employees?
For the current 54 employees of the plant, the situation is precarious. An additional collective dismissal of 25 people would involve specific procedures according to Swiss federal law: at least 30 days' notice, consultation with employees, and notification to the competent authority (SECO). Dismissed employees would be entitled to unemployment benefits according to the Unemployment Insurance (AD/AC), up to the 150 days provided by federal law.
The context is particularly delicate because the production activity has been halted for months: it remains uncertain whether the remaining employees are still receiving a regular salary or are in situations of partial unemployment. The concordat procedure should provide transparency, but the fact remains that two previous attempts to sell the brand have failed, raising doubts about the feasibility of a positive solution in the short term. The waiting period could be extended, prolonging occupational uncertainty.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Rights and resources for employees
Employees of Bally involved in collective dismissals have specific rights according to Swiss law. First, they must receive written notice of at least 30 days for ordinary dismissals (or the contractual duration if higher). In the case of collective dismissal (affecting ≥10 people within 30 days), the company must notify the Employment Service of the Canton of Ticino and consult the affected employees, possibly through their union representatives.
Once the employment relationship ends, employees can apply for unemployment benefits at the cantonal unemployment office in Ticino. Unemployment Insurance (AD) generally covers up to 150 days of benefits (extendable for employees over 55 years old). The amount of the benefit varies based on the previous salary and provides fundamental protection during the occupational transition.
Additionally, the Canton of Ticino and SECO offer concrete support for active job searching: professional counseling, retraining courses, support in CV writing and job applications. Employees of Caslano should contact the regional employment office in Ticino promptly to access these services and begin the process of finding new opportunities.
### Relocation prospects
The luxury footwear sector in Switzerland is limited and specialized. However, the 54-79 affected employees have transferable skills: quality craftsmanship, production management, administration, logistics, and quality control. The job market in the Ticino regions remains dynamic in other sectors: hospitality, healthcare, construction, small retail, and services. [Consult available job listings](nav:jobs) to explore concrete opportunities in your canton.
In the meantime, it is crucial that remaining employees at Bally closely follow the developments of the bankruptcy procedure. The status of the search for a buyer will be decisive: a positive takeover would mean occupational continuity, while a failure to sell could lead to the total liquidation of the activity. In parallel, employees should verify that their contributions to professional pension funds (LPP/BVG) have been correctly paid up to the date of dismissal. In case of employer insolvency, the LPP guarantee fund protects acquired rights, but it is advisable to contact the cantonal supervisory authority to verify the personal situation. If you are a Bally employee or monitoring a similar situation, register with the unemployment office and [evaluate your opportunities with our salary calculator and financial planning](nav:calculator) to best structure your AVS/LPP contributions during the transition period.

item.title: Medical research in Ticino: from the laboratory to the patient
item.description: The USI Research Day in Lugano: 200 scientific contributions on how innovation accelerates the path from discovery to treatment.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Research Day on September 4 in Lugano: 200+ scientific contributions - Medical research accelerates access to innovative treatments and therapies - EOC, USI, SUPSI, IRB: Ticino attracts talents from Switzerland and the world - Artificial intelligence applied to medicine: the fastest-growing sector
## Key facts - **What**: Research and Innovation Day in Human Medicine of Italian Switzerland - When: September 4, 2026 (15th edition) - Where: USI East Campus, Lugano - Who: EOC, USI, SUPSI, IRB, IOR - Contributions: Over 200 scientific abstracts presented - Participants: Approximately 300+ attendees on average - Strong sectors: Oncology, cardiology, neurology, immunology
---
On September 4, the Research and Innovation Day in Human Medicine of Italian Switzerland returns to the USI East Campus in Lugano, marking its fifteenth edition. Over 200 scientific contributions will highlight the present and future of medicine in the canton, with more than 300 participants expected. This event summarizes a now-established reality: in Switzerland, and particularly in Ticino, medical research determines timely access to innovative treatments.
"Having a hospital where research is conducted can mean accessing a new drug, diagnostic technology, or innovative therapy sooner," explains Professor Alessandro Ceschi, head of the Medical Training and Research Area at EOC. "Conducting research creates a culture within a hospital of staying updated with the latest evidence, basing decisions on efficacy proofs, and constantly questioning how to treat patients better."
### Acceleration from the laboratory to the patient
The cycle separating laboratory discovery from clinical treatment has significantly shortened in recent years. Ceschi highlights that this acceleration is made possible by three key factors: a deeper understanding of biology and diseases, which allows for more precise therapeutic targets; the ability to accurately select the type of patient suitable for that treatment; and new technologies and more efficient processes. "In the past, various steps, even at the regulatory authority level, were done one after the other. Today, more processes are carried out in parallel, which greatly shortens the timelines," Ceschi notes.
Among the most established research sectors in the canton are oncology, cardiology, and neurology, as well as immunology and translational research. A field poised for significant growth is artificial intelligence applied to medicine. "It is gaining traction in various areas and accelerating the development of new therapies and diagnostic methodologies," observes Ceschi. This virtuous connection between basic research and clinical application exactly represents the value that the Research Day aims to highlight: transforming scientific discoveries into concrete benefits for Swiss patients. ### The Ticino research ecosystem
Ticino has a solid institutional network for biomedical research. In addition to the EoC (Cantonal Hospital Authority), which provides the clinical structure, there are the University of Italian Switzerland (USI) with its Faculty of Biomedical Sciences, the Research Institute in Biomedicine (IRB), the Oncological Institute of Radiotherapy (IOR) and the Professional University School of Italian Switzerland (SUPSI). This ecosystem is not only a strategic value for local patients, but also a powerful tool for attracting qualified talent.
"Being able to attract doctors and other high-value professionals from other regions of Switzerland or the world means bringing skills here that then benefit patients," continues Ceschi. The international reputation of Ticino research did not come from nothing: behind it there is a project built over the years, as recalled by Greta Guarda, deputy dean of the USI Faculty of Biomedical Sciences. "A precedent has been created that showed that it is possible to do high-level research in Ticino. Today, so many people are drawn to these very examples.” Among the examples that Guarda cites is Antonio Lanzavecchia, who chose Bellinzona to develop world-class research, thus establishing a model that continues to inspire researchers and investors.

According to Ceschi, "financing research is also a forward-looking political decision." Investing in biomedicine means not only improving the quality of care but also attracting skills and creating qualified jobs in the territory. "Our interest as a hospital is to ensure that patients can benefit more quickly from the most effective and safe therapies."
The statement emphasizes how medical research generates benefits that go beyond the healthcare field: specialized employment, territorial prestige, ability to retain and attract talent. However, as Guarda reminds us, research requires a perspective of continuity. "Research and the academic world develop over longer periods than a typical political term. Patience and foresight are needed." This means that public decision-makers must understand how today's investments in research will produce employment, health, and economic benefits over time spans of 5-10 years, not just over a legislative term.
### Research Day: agenda and awards
The event on September 4 will welcome over 300 participants and present more than 200 scientific contributions from Italian Switzerland. The event is structured to facilitate dialogue between researchers, clinicians, nurses, and computational professionals. At the end of the day, three significant awards will be presented:
- **Dick Marty Award**: awarded for the best publication in oncology, recognizing excellence in a key sector for Ticino - Fidinam Fellowship: funds a research experience abroad, allowing Ticino researchers to acquire international skills and bring them back to the territory - Awards for the best scientific presentations: encourage young researchers to disseminate their results
This structure of awards and recognitions illustrates how the Ticino research system is oriented not only towards scientific production but also towards the training of new talents, the circulation of skills, and integration with the global scientific community. For those interested in [job opportunities in the biomedical research sector](nav:jobs), consulting specialized selection platforms allows you to discover open positions at research centers, university hospitals, and Swiss institutes in the diagnostic, pharmacological, and experimental clinical fields.

item.title: Cantonal taxes in the canton of Vaud: rates and deductions
item.description: 3-tier tax system, progressive rates for income brackets, allowable deductions and official portal of the canton of Vaud for declarations.
item.content:encoded:
## In short - 3-level system: federal + cantonal + municipal multiplier - Progressive rates according to income and wealth brackets - Authorized deductions (3a, professional expenses, mortgage interest) - Declaration by 31 May of the year following the tax period
## Key facts - **What**: Cantonal and municipal taxes on income and wealth in the canton of Vaud - Where: Canton of Vaud, Romandy, Switzerland - System: 3 tax levels (federal, cantonal, municipal) - Structure: Progressive brackets defined by the canton + variable municipal multiplier - Portal: Cantonal tax administration publishes rates, multipliers, and forms
The canton of Vaud applies a system of cantonal and municipal taxes structured according to Swiss federal legislation: three levels of taxation (federal, cantonal, municipal). Unlike countries with a centralized tax system, Switzerland grants each canton the autonomy to define rates, brackets, and authorized deductions. The municipalities of Vaud subsequently add a percentage multiplier to the cantonal taxes, which results in variations even between neighboring municipalities.
Vaud cantonal taxes apply to personal income, wealth, and, for business owners, business profits. Gross income is reduced by authorized deductions (pension contributions, professional expenses, mortgage interest, donations); the resulting net income is taxed at progressive rates defined by the canton. Two residents with the same income in two Vaud municipalities may pay slightly different amounts, as the municipal multiplier varies from one municipality to another.
### The progressive bracket system
The rates of the canton of Vaud increase by income brackets: lower incomes pay reduced percentages, higher incomes pay increasing rates. A resident can consult the updated brackets annually on the portal of the cantonal tax administration. In addition to income, there is a separate wealth tax (real estate, accounts, investments) also divided into value brackets. The municipal multiplier — a percentage coefficient set by each municipality — applies to both income tax and wealth tax. Two Vaud municipalities can have different multipliers (for example, one at 120%, the other at 135%), so the taxpayer's residence significantly affects the final tax. The cantonal administration publishes an official table annually with brackets, rates, and municipal multipliers. The income tax return must be filed by the end of May of the year following the tax period, unless there are official extensions. The canton of Vaud recognises an extensive catalogue of authorised deductions, in line with Swiss federal law and with specific cantonal additions. The main deductions common to all Swiss cantons, including Vaud, include payments to the third pension pillar (3a), up to the annual ceiling set federally and indexed each year.
Those who practice a self-employed or freelance profession can deduct documented professional expenses and costs of continuous training. Property owners deduct interest expense on mortgages related to the primary residence. Compulsory contributions to unemployment (AD) and accident (LAINF/AC) insurance, already withheld in the paycheck, are recognised as deductions. Donations to recognised non-profit organisations are deductible up to a cantonal ceiling.
### Check deductions in Vaud
As the federal and cantonal regulatory framework is frequently updated, it is crucial that every resident consults the official canton Vaud portal before filing taxes. The site of the cantonal tax administration provides an exhaustive list of authorized deductions, the maximum amounts applicable, the conditions of application and the documents to be attached. Many deductions require supporting documentation (social security contribution certificates, mortgage statements, donation receipts); without this documentation the deduction is not accepted.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). Tax declaration in the canton of Vaud follows a standardized procedure, made easier by the online services of the cantonal tax administration. The general deadline for submitting the declaration is May 31 of the year following the tax period (May 31, 2025 for the 2024 income, and so on). Late declaration incurs an administrative fine; it is therefore important to respect the deadline, unless official extensions are granted by the canton. Step-by-step: how to declare in Vaud Before declaring, the resident must gather income certificates (pay slips, self-employment certificates), bank account statements, receipts for deductible expenses (donations, mortgage interest, pension contributions), and asset documents (deposit statements, property value declarations). The cantonal administration provides paper forms and fillable online versions. The form requires personal data, income by source, itemized deductions, declared assets, and estimated tax calculation based on cantonal brackets and the municipal multiplier. The declaration can be submitted online via the cantonal portal, by mail, or in person at the cantonal tax office; online submission reduces processing times. The cantonal administration reviews the declaration and, if correct, issues an official assessment with the amount due. In case of discrepancies or lack of documentation, the taxpayer receives a request for clarification. The official website of the Vaud cantonal tax administration (www.vd.ch — dedicated tax section) hosts all necessary information: updated brackets, rates, and municipal multipliers, list of authorized deductions, declaration forms, payment deadline guide, FAQ, and local office contacts. It is advisable to consult the official portal before each declaration to verify any regulatory or administrative changes. Many residents also use private tax consulting services or seek help from unions and professional associations, which often offer free assistance in filling out the forms. For a preliminary estimate of your tax burden in the canton of Vaud, you can use the online [tax calculator](nav:calculator), which applies the municipal multipliers and updated rates for a quick assessment.

item.title: Open business Thurgau: trade register and costs
item.description: Practical guide to setting up a business in the canton of Thurgau: registration procedures, legal forms, federal and cantonal taxation, SUVA obligations and social security.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - In Switzerland, business owners must register with the cantonal trade register within 30 days. - Taxation on 3 levels: federal (IFD), cantonal and municipal. - SUVA and LAMal mandatory for employees; AVS/LPP for pensions.
## Key facts - **What**: Registration in the trade register for new business - Where: Canton Thurgau (cantonal administration) - Who: Natural and legal persons (different legal forms available) - When: Within 30 days from the start of the activity - Taxes: 3 contemporary levels (federal, cantonal, municipal)
Anyone wishing to open a business in the canton of Thurgau must register with the commercial register as in every Swiss canton. The procedure is governed by federal and cantonal rules governing legal forms, taxation and insurance obligations. Taxation follows a system divided into three levels: direct federal tax (DFI), cantonal and municipal tax, each with its own rates.
The canton of Thurgau sets its own rates independently of other cantons; the municipalities, in turn, apply multipliers on the cantonal tax, varying the final tax burden. Those who are about to start a company must consider not only the registration costs (variable by canton), but also the tax structure that will affect them in the years to come, social security contributions, and mandatory insurance for employees.
### Registration in the commercial register In Switzerland, the register of ### Taxation at three levels: federal, cantonal, and municipal The fiscal aspect is central to every entrepreneurial decision. In Switzerland, taxation operates simultaneously at three levels: federal, cantonal, and municipal. Each level has its own competencies and rates, creating a complex but transparent structure.
At the federal level, the Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV) manages the federal direct tax (FDT) and the value-added tax (VAT). These taxes are uniform throughout Switzerland according to federal laws; no canton can modify them. VAT is particularly relevant for those with annual turnover above a federal threshold: registration with the VAT register becomes mandatory and requires invoicing services with VAT applied.
At the cantonal level, the Canton of Thurgau sets its own rates for corporate income tax, independently of Zurich, Bern, or Geneva. Each cantonal administration has its own tax laws and multipliers that vary significantly. Municipalities, in turn, apply a multiplier to the cantonal tax, effectively increasing the total burden. Two identical businesses, one in Frauenfeld and the other in a neighboring municipality of the Canton of Thurgau, may pay very different amounts in taxes.
### Federal and Cantonal Competencies The FTA/ESTV manages the FDT and VAT at the national level; cantonal administrations manage cantonal and municipal taxation and local tax incentives. Those opening a business in the Canton of Thurgau must register with the Thurgau cantonal administration for corporate income tax and with the municipal tax office of the municipality where the business is located. The Thurgau cantonal administration provides information on the current rates; it is advisable to consult them to understand the exact tax structure of your situation.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Insurance and Pension Obligations Whoever opens a business with employees must comply with strictly defined insurance and pension obligations in Switzerland. These obligations ensure the protection of workers and the stability of the national pension system.
**Accident Insurance (SUVA)** If the company employs at least one person, registration with SUVA (Swiss National Accident Insurance) is mandatory. SUVA covers professional risks — workplace accidents and occupational diseases — of employees. Premiums are calculated based on the economic sector and the number of employees; they vary significantly between a manufacturing industry and a professional office.
Health Insurance (LAMal) It is not a direct company obligation, but every resident in Switzerland, including employees, must subscribe to their own health insurance (LAMal/KVG) within 3 months of arrival in the canton or the start of employment. It is a private coverage with premiums varying by canton, age bracket, and chosen deductible. The Canton of Thurgau, like all cantons, offers subsidies (premium reductions) for insured persons with low income.
Pension: AVS/AI and LPP On every salary paid to an employee, the company pays contributions to the Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance (AVS/AI) and, if the employee has a coordinated salary above a certain threshold, to the Occupational Pension Scheme (LPP/BVG). The AVS/AI contributions are 5.3% of the gross salary for the employee; the employer pays the equivalent (for a total of 10.6%). The disability insurance (AI) and loss of earnings allowance (IPG) are part of the same AVS/AI contribution. The LPP covers the complementary occupational pension and the contributions vary based on the employee's age and coordinated salary.
### Step-by-Step Procedure 1. Choose the legal form (sole proprietorship, simple partnership, collective partnership, limited liability company, public limited company) — consult the Thurgau cantonal administration for the specific minimum capital requirements for each form. 2. Contact the cantonal commercial register (Canton of Thurgau) for registration; it must occur within 30 days from the start of the activity. 3. Register with the Federal Tax Administration for VAT if the annual turnover exceeds the federal threshold defined by Swiss VAT regulations. 4. Register the company with the Thurgau cantonal administration for cantonal and municipal taxation. 5. If you employ staff, request registration with SUVA for accident insurance. 6. Inform your employees of the obligation to subscribe to health insurance (LAMal) within 3 months of the start of employment. 7. Set up the payment of AVS/AI/LPP contributions through your local compensation fund.
To accurately estimate the initial and recurring costs of your activity based on the legal form, sector, and number of expected employees, you can use the [business cost calculator](nav:calculator) which takes into account the Swiss tax structure.

item.title: St. Gallen permit: validity and extension
item.description: Short-term permit L up to 1 year, renewal procedures, constraints on the employer, transformation into permit B. Practical guide.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The short-term L permit is valid for up to 1 year in Switzerland - It is strictly tied to the employer specified at the time of issuance - Renewal is not automatic: request 2-3 months before expiration - Can be converted to a B residence permit after 12-24 months of regular stay
## Key facts - **What**: Temporary residence permit for foreign workers - When: Valid for up to 1 year from the date of issuance - Where: Applicable in Switzerland, including the Canton of St. Gallen - Who: Regulated by the SEM (State Secretariat for Migration) - Legal basis: Federal Law on Foreign Nationals (LStrI) and cantonal ordinances - Renewal: Formal request before expiration, case-by-case evaluation
The short-term L permit represents the most common form of temporary stay in Switzerland for foreign workers intending to exercise a professional activity for a limited period. This permit is regulated at the federal level by the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) and issued by the competent cantonal authorities, including the Canton of St. Gallen. The main feature is the maximum validity of 1 year: the document expires automatically at the end of this period if not renewed or converted into another type of permit.
A decisive aspect of the L permit is the tie to the employer. The holder can work exclusively for the employer specified at the time of issuance and for the positions declared in the application. A change of employer requires a modification request submitted jointly by the interested parties to the cantonal authorities. This tie significantly differentiates the L permit from higher category permits, such as the B (residence) permit, which allows greater professional freedom. If you wish to explore job opportunities in Switzerland, you can consult [specialized ads](nav:jobs).
### The federal system of foreign permits
Switzerland manages the stay of foreigners through four main categories: L (short-term, up to 1 year), B (residence, renewable), C (permanent residence) and G (cross-border commuter). The L permit represents the first step for those intending to work temporarily in Switzerland. The Canton of St. Gallen, like all cantons, applies this federal system: the cantonal migration offices manage issuance, renewal, and modifications in coordination with the SEM.
The duration of the L permit generally corresponds to the length of the employment contract signed, with a maximum of 1 calendar year. If the contract is for a fixed term and expires before the end of the year, the L permit follows automatically. If the employer intends to continue the relationship, the holder must submit a renewal request before expiration. Once expired, the permit cannot be recovered: the holder loses the right to reside and work legally in Switzerland. ### Conditions and formal procedure for extension
The extension of the L permit does not happen automatically. About 2-3 months before the expiry date, the permit holder and the employer must jointly submit a formal renewal application to the cantonal authorities of the Canton of St. Gallen. The documentation must include: an updated copy of the employment contract, an official statement from the employer confirming the continuation of the employment relationship and the absence of regulatory violations during the previous stay period.
The cantonal authorities will evaluate specific criteria before approving the renewal: - Continuity and validity of the employment contract; - Adequacy of the salary according to Swiss standards; - Persistence of the initial conditions (the position remains a priority and cannot be filled by available Swiss personnel); - Absence of legal violations during the previous stay (violations of labor law, administrative or criminal problems).
If all conditions remain satisfied, the L permit is renewed for an additional period, generally up to 1 year. If the renewal application is not submitted on time or is denied, the holder usually has a grace period of 30-60 days to leave Switzerland. Failure to renew exposes to administrative expulsion procedures and registration in records that make it difficult to obtain future authorizations. To assess whether your income during your stay is consistent with the [cost of living in Switzerland](nav:cost-of-living), consult specialized resources.
### Transition from L permit to B permit: stability and professional freedom
An alternative to simply extending the L permit is transitioning to a B permit (residence). The B permit offers more stable stay conditions: it is renewable for periods of 5 years and is less strictly tied to a single employer. With a B permit, the holder enjoys greater freedom in changing jobs and stronger legal protection against expulsion, especially in case of temporary unemployment.
The transition from L to B is not automatic and depends on federal and cantonal criteria. Generally, it is possible after 12-24 months of legal and continuous stay with a valid L permit. The holder must also demonstrate a stable economic and professional situation: regular employment, sufficient income, no debts to Swiss authorities, and compliance with laws.
The evaluation for transitioning to B is more in-depth than a simple extension of L. The SEM involves the cantonal offices in a comprehensive review of the personal and work situation. Positive elements include an open-ended contract, correct tax documentation, and regular enrollment in social contributions (AVS/AI/LPP). If approved, the B permit is usually issued for 5 years and is subject to automatic renewal if the conditions remain satisfied. During this process, understanding tax obligations is essential: consult the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return) to avoid penalties.
### Scenario: changing employer during the L permit
If you intend to change employers during the validity of the L permit, the procedure depends on the remaining time. If there are 2-3 months left, the old employer, the new employer, and the holder can jointly submit a request to modify the permit, indicating the new employer and the duties. The cantonal authorities will evaluate the compatibility with local economic conditions and the labor market.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Step-by-step procedure for renewal in the Canton of St. Gallen
If you hold a permit L and wish to renew it, follow this ordered procedure:
Step 1: Check the expiration date. Consult your original permit L to identify the exact expiration date. Plan the renewal well in advance: it is crucial to submit the application at least 2-3 months before to avoid administrative complications.
Step 2: Notify your employer. Inform your employer of your intention to renew the permit and ask for their cooperation in preparing the documentation. The employer must formally sign the continuation of the employment relationship.
Step 3: Gather the necessary documents. Prepare: - Recent and signed copy of the employment contract (or official letter from the employer confirming the continuation); - Valid original permit L; - Valid identity document (passport or national identity card); - Recent certificate of residence (from the municipality of residence in the Canton of St. Gallen); - Written statement from the employer confirming: (a) continuation of the employment relationship, (b) absence of regulatory violations, (c) regular payment of salary, (d) compliance with workplace safety regulations.
Step 4: Submit the application to the competent office. Contact the migration office of the Canton of St. Gallen competent for your district of residence. Check with the office whether it is possible to submit the application online or if personal presentation is required. Some offices require a prior appointment.
**Step 5: Await evaluation.** The cantonal authorities, in coordination with the SEM, will examine the application. The processing time generally varies from 2 to 4 weeks. A face-to-face interview with a migration office official may be necessary.
Step 6: Receive the result. Once the evaluation is complete, you will receive an official communication. If the renewal is approved, the new permit L will be issued (again for a maximum of 1 year). If the application is denied, you will receive a written decision with the reasons and possibilities of appeal.
### Critical deadlines and consequences of non-renewal
Not renewing the permit L before the expiration date exposes you to severe legal consequences. Once the permit expires, the stay becomes automatically irregular: the holder loses the right to reside and work legally. This can lead to an administrative expulsion procedure, registration in expulsion records that make it difficult to obtain a new permit in the future, and financial penalties or criminal proceedings if the irregular stay is continuous.
It is not possible to renew a permit after it has expired. If the permit expires without renewal, the holder must leave Switzerland and, if they wish to return to work, must submit a completely new application from abroad, with all the associated times and risks.
### Verify the tax and contribution situation after renewal
Once the permit L has been renewed, it is useful to verify the regularity of your contribution and tax situation. In Switzerland, workers with a permit L are subject to the same social contribution and tax obligations as Swiss residents, including AVS/AI/IPG contributions (pension and disability insurance) and, if employed, enrollment in a pension fund (LPP/BVG) if provided by the company.
To understand the impact of your gross salary on federal, cantonal, and municipal taxes, as well as the net monthly amount, you can use the [salary and tax calculator](nav:calculator) that simulates your treatment based on personal data, the canton of residence (St. Gallen), and the income category. This is useful to verify that your employer is treating you in accordance with Swiss regulations and to plan your medium-term budget.

item.title: Opening a business in Thurgau: costs and procedure
item.description: Step-by-step guide: legal forms, trade register registration, federal/cantonal taxes, AVS/LPP/LAMal contributions and insurance obligations to start a business in Switzerland.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Three tax levels: federal, cantonal and municipal (multiplier on cantonal) - AVS/AI 5.3% for employees, LPP 7–18% according to age from coordinated salary - Mandatory registration in the commercial register before starting activity - LAMal mandatory, deductibles from 300 to 2500 CHF per year, premiums per canton/region
## Key facts - **What**: Complete procedure to open a company, corporation or other legal form - Where: Canton of Thurgau (same procedures throughout Switzerland) - Who: Cantonal registration offices, AFC/ESTV, municipal administration, UFAS/BSV pension - Legal forms: Sole proprietorship, general partnership, limited partnership, SA, Sàrl, cooperative - Mandatory contributions: AVS/AI, LAINF (if employees), LPP, LAMal - Tax levels: IFD federal + cantonal tax + municipal
Starting a business in the Canton of Thurgau follows the same procedures and regulations that apply throughout the Swiss Confederation. Whether you choose to open a sole proprietorship, a limited liability company or a corporation, the administrative and tax path remains structured around three fundamental elements: the choice of legal form, registration in the commercial register, and compliance with tax and insurance obligations. Swiss taxation operates at three distinct levels — federal, cantonal and municipal — and each canton has its own laws and different tax multipliers, although the basic principles remain uniform at the national level.
### Legal forms: which to choose
The choice of legal form is the first decisive step. A sole proprietorship allows for agile management and no federal minimum capital requirement, but the owner is personally liable with their own assets. A general partnership binds several partners in joint liability. A limited partnership separates limited partners (limited liability) from managers. A corporation (SA) requires a minimum number of shareholders and capital, offering asset protection through limited liability. A limited liability company (Sàrl) is a hybrid form, suitable for small businesses with multiple owners. Cooperatives remain an option for collaborative models. No form is absolutely better: the choice depends on the number of partners, available capital, the nature of the activity and the desired level of asset protection. A cantonal accountant or notary can guide you in making the most appropriate decision according to your specific case.
Before any other registration, consult the commercial register office of the Canton of Thurgau to verify the specific requirements of the chosen legal form and the procedures for depositing the constitutive documents. Registration in the register is mandatory and must take place before starting the activity. Once registered, the company acquires legal personality and tax rights/obligations. ### Three-tier taxation and tax registration

 In Switzerland, every entrepreneur is subject to three levels of taxation: the direct federal tax (DFD) administered by the Federal Customs and Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV), the cantonal tax administered by the Thurgau authorities, and the municipal tax, which is calculated using a multiplier applied to the cantonal tax base. The multiplier varies from municipality to municipality: one municipality may have a low multiplier, while a neighboring municipality may have a higher multiplier. This three-tier structure means that the overall tax burden depends both on the chosen geographic location within the canton (such as municipality) and on the applicable federal and cantonal tax rates. There is no federal minimum wage in Switzerland, although some cantons have introduced their own at the cantonal or municipal level: check whether the Canton of Thurgau has minimum wage regulations that apply to you.

 Registration with the Federal Customs Administration for VAT and other federal obligations is mandatory if your annual turnover exceeds the VAT registration threshold (annually indexed amount; see AFC/ESTV for the current figure). If you’re just starting out, you can self-register even below the threshold. Cantonal and municipal tax registration is carried out through the respective Thurgau offices, generally at the same time or shortly after registration in the commercial register. Within the timeframe established by the canton (check deadlines),
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Step-by-step procedure to start a business
Once you have decided on the legal form, follow these steps in sequence:
**1. Constitution and documents**: Draw up or have drawn up the constitutive documents (articles of association, statutes, partnership agreement depending on the form). Have the signatures authenticated by the cantonal notary if necessary.
2. Registration with the commercial register: Submit the original documents to the commercial registration office of your canton of Thurgau. Check the official website for the procedures (paper, electronic, opening hours) and registration fees (which vary according to canton and form). Generally, you must indicate: business name, legal form, address of the registered office, partners/managers, business sector.
3. Obtaining the IDE number: Once registered, you will receive the company identification number (IDE) — a unique code to identify the company in the federal registers. Keep this number: it will be needed for all future tax obligations.
4. Federal VAT registration (AFC/ESTV): If you expect turnover above the VAT threshold, or if you voluntarily register, complete the registration form with AFC/ESTV. You can do this online on the federal portal or on paper. You will receive a VAT number.
5. Canton-commune tax registration: Contact the tax office of the Canton of Thurgau and your municipality. They will ask for a copy of the commercial registration, IDE, tax IDE if applicable, and information about partners/managers. You will complete a declaration on the form of management and source of income.
6. AVS/AI registration: If you are self-employed, you must register with the AVS compensation fund of your canton. Provide a copy of the commercial registration, extract from the register, and personal data. You will receive an AVS number for self-employed management with a progressive contribution rate.
7. Accident insurance (LAINF): If you hire employees, you must take out accident insurance with SUVA or a registered private insurer. If you are a sole proprietorship without employees, LAINF is optional but recommended. Register before hiring your first employee.
8. Professional pension scheme (LPP/BVG): If you hire employees, you must affiliate the company with a pension fund (pension institution, foundation, collective solution, insurance). They provide the policy, regulations, and guide you through the payment procedures. Check with an accountant which form is most efficient for your case.
9. Business bank account: Open a current account with a Swiss bank in the name of the company (provide constitutive documents, IDE, copy of commercial registration). Necessary to separate personal and business transactions.
10. LAMal subscription: You and any employees must take out compulsory health insurance with a health insurance fund. You can choose from providers in your canton/region. Couples/families get reduced rates if they sign up together. Check for cantonal subsidies for low incomes.
11. Accounting and first declaration: Open an accounting register (mandatory for companies; also recommended for sole proprietorships). Record each transaction. Keep invoices, receipts, bank statements. Within the deadlines set by the canton (generally within 3–4 months of the calendar year), you must submit the tax return (cantonal model) attaching the balance sheet (if accounting obligation) or simplified statement.
⚠️ Deadlines: The procedures listed above have different timelines: commercial registration is immediate (hours/days), federal VAT takes 1–2 weeks, AVS/AI similarly, cantonal taxes within 1 month, LAINF and LPP must be completed before hiring the first employee. Do not postpone these obligations: the authorities charge penalties for omissions.
### Useful tools and next steps
To calculate the AVS/AI and LPP contribution burden on your projected income, use the [salary and pension calculator](nav:calculator). Remember that contributions change every year (indexed figures). To delve into the second and third pillars and plan your pension as a self-employed person, consult the [Pensions and Provision](nav:pension) section. To understand the LAMal options and compare premiums, use the [health insurance tool](nav:health).
Finally, rely on a cantonal tax advisor or accountant for an audit of the chosen legal form, tax optimization, and administrative-accounting management. The initial investment in consulting will save you costly mistakes along the way.

item.title: Inheritance and donation tax: Svitto guide
item.description: Inheritance and gift taxes in the Canton of Schwyz: rates, exemptions, declaration, terms. Complete guide on wealth taxation.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - In the Canton of Schwyz, as in other Swiss cantons, specific taxes apply to inheritances and donations - Tax rates vary depending on the degree of kinship and the amount transferred - Each canton regulates its own tax, with common principles such as the exemption of the spouse
## Key facts - **What**: Taxes on inheritances (succession) and transfers of assets between living individuals (donations) - Where: Canton of Schwyz (with specific cantonal rules) - Who: Heirs and beneficiaries of donations, according to the degree of kinship - Levels: Federal, cantonal, and communal (3 levels of taxation in Switzerland) - Principle: Cantonal autonomy in defining tax rates and exemptions
### Taxation of asset transfers in Schwyz In the Canton of Schwyz, as in every Swiss canton, the transfer of assets — whether by succession (in case of death) or by donation (transfer between living individuals) — is subject to specific cantonal taxes. The Swiss tax system, with its 3 levels (federal, cantonal, and communal), grants cantons the autonomy to define their own tax rates, exemptions, and procedures for these taxes.
Unlike income taxes, where there is a uniform federal tax (Federal Direct Tax, FDT), inheritance and donation taxes remain entirely in the hands of the cantons. This autonomy means that the Canton of Schwyz has its own regulations, different from those of other cantons such as Zurich, Bern, or Basel.
Inheritance taxes apply to the transfer of assets following a person's death. Donation taxes, on the other hand, tax transfers of assets between living individuals. Although they operate in different contexts, both follow the same principle: the degree of kinship between the deceased (or donor) and the heir (or beneficiary of the donation) determines whether full, partial exemptions, or tax rates apply.
The Canton of Schwyz, like many Swiss cantons, generally provides significant exemptions for spouses and direct descendants. This means that in many cases, the transfer of assets between these individuals is not subject to taxation, or is subject to very low tax rates. Filing the inheritance declaration with the tax authorities is a fundamental obligation that risks exposing to penalties if not complied with. Heirs must submit complete and accurate documentation to the cantonal tax office, respecting the deadlines set by cantonal regulations. ### How the cantonal system differentiates transfers
The legislation of the Canton of Schwyz explicitly distinguishes between different categories of heirs and beneficiaries, applying differentiated rates. The rates depend on the degree of kinship: the surviving spouse and children (direct descendants) usually enjoy total or partial exemptions, while more distant relatives (sisters, brothers, cousins) face higher tax rates. Family outsiders often face the highest rates.
Each Swiss canton organizes this taxation autonomously. Some cantons have chosen to completely abolish inheritance and gift taxes in recent decades. Others maintain structured systems with exemptions and progressive rates. The Canton of Schwyz follows the tradition of an orderly taxation, with established principles.
The declaration of inheritance is a formal obligation with the cantonal tax authority. This declaration must occur within specific deadlines — usually a few months after the person's death. Failure to meet these deadlines can result in tax penalties. Similarly, significant gifts must be declared within specific periods, and the beneficiary of the gift is required to communicate what they have received to the authority.
A crucial aspect is that the Swiss system does not provide for a federal inheritance tax. The Confederation does not directly tax property transfers. Taxation remains the exclusive prerogative of the cantons, which in turn can delegate part of the taxation to the municipalities. In Schwyz, this structure means that in addition to the actual cantonal rate, municipal taxes can be added, often calculated as a multiplier on the cantonal amount.
For those planning their estate and wanting to understand the tax impact of transfers, [using a tax calculator](nav:calculator) can help evaluate different scenarios, although professional advice is always recommended.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Operational procedure and deadlines in the Canton of Schwyz
In the event of a succession in the Canton of Schwyz, the heirs are required to submit a declaration of succession to the cantonal tax office within the deadline set by cantonal legislation (typically between 3 and 6 months from the date of death, depending on the circumstances). This declaration must include a detailed inventory of the deceased's estate, with current valuations of real estate, bank accounts, securities, life insurance, and other assets.
The declaration must be signed by at least one heir—often the eldest or the one acting as the representative of the heirs—and submitted along with supporting documentation:
- Death certificate (extract from the municipal office) - Will or notarial document (if available) - Extract from the commercial register (if the deceased was a business owner) - Bank statements and investment documentation - Certified real estate valuations
The cantonal tax office of Schwyz evaluates the declaration and calculates the tax due. If the heirs benefit from exemptions (spouse, children), the office applies these deductions to the taxable amount. The calculated tax becomes due according to the methods and deadlines set by the canton.
For donations, the procedure is similar but anticipated: the donor and the beneficiary must declare the transfer within specific deadlines, allowing the authority to verify the amount and apply the correct rates and exemptions. Consulting a tax or notarial advisor is strongly recommended, especially for significant estates or complex situations. The cantonal offices maintain informative guides and downloadable forms on their official websites. To understand exactly the rates, exemptions, and specific deadlines applicable in the Canton of Schwyz, it is essential to contact the cantonal tax administration directly. A [tax calculator](nav:calculator) is useful for estimating the tax impact of estate transfers, but it does not replace professional advice.
